label: Approaching (2028–2032 expected)
rationale: No fusion plant has yet delivered sustained electricity to a grid, and engineering breakeven is unproven. 2025 brought record progress (NIF Q=4.13, WEST 22-minute plasma, Helion beginning construction of its Orion plant, CFS raising $863M), with Helion and CFS leading toward 2028-2032 grid timelines if private schedules hold.

label: Distant
rationale: First-of-a-kind fusion plants are projected above $150/MWh, versus $50-78/MWh averages for wind, solar and gas. Nth-of-a-kind plants at $50-100/MWh are plausible only in the 2040s-2050s; all fusion LCOE figures are projections since no plant operates.

label: ⚠️ Mixed
rationale: Renewable generation costs have collapsed (solar LCOE $43/MWh, -90% since 2010), but wholesale prices remain volatile and rose in H1 2025 (EU ~$90/MWh, US ~$48/MWh). Fusion remains commercially unproven, with first plants expected to exceed current nuclear costs.

label: Progressing: no fusion on any grid yet; Helion Orion under construction, ETA ~2035
rationale: No fusion plant delivers electricity to a grid and no device has shown net electricity (Helion missed its 2024 target), but Helion began building its Orion plant in July 2025 and five funded programmes target commercial power between 2028 and 2035. Treating the first plant as the first success among those programmes, with proponent dates discounted ~2x and per-concept success odds, gives a median of ~2035 (80% range 2030-2051), bracketed by the fission reference class (first chain reaction to grid power in 11.5-15 years, i.e. 2034.5-2038 from NIF ignition) and by NIF's +54%/yr yield trend. A median within 10 years with measurable progress is yellow; it is not green because the median is beyond 5 years and no net-electricity precursor or independent corroboration exists.

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: measurable progress (first commercial plant under construction, record fusion gain, funded programmes) and median ETA 2035 <= made_at + 10 years. Not green: median > 5 years, no demonstrated precursor at relevant scale (no net electricity from any device) and no non-proponent corroboration. Not achieved: no verified achievement of fusion electricity on a grid

eta.method: discounted proponent dates (first-success Monte Carlo over 5 programmes) + structural floor + reference class (fission) + driver trend (NIF yield) cross-check
eta.calc: Gap: 0 MWh fusion on any grid; no net electricity yet (helion-missed-2024-rv); best gain NIF Q=4.13 (8.6 MJ/2.08 MJ, nif-q-4-13-rv) but wall-plug ~0.03 (~300 MJ laser draw, bg) -> ~87x yield gap to a plant at 40% conversion. Floor: Orion earthworks Jul 2025 + ~3-4 yr build/commissioning -> no sustained delivery before ~2029. MC (N=200k): each programme year = stated + (target - stated) x lognormal factor (median 2x, shared sd 0.25 + own 0.30), success odds Helion 2028/0.5, CFS ARC ~2032/0.6, TAE ~2032/0.3, Tokamak Energy ~2035/0.3, Focused-Biblis 2035/0.25 -> first-of-any P(2030) 9%, P(2035) 44%, P(2036.0) 51%, P(2040) 71%, P(2050) 89%; p10 2030.1, p50 2035.9, p90 2051.5. Reference class (bg): CP-1 1942 -> Obninsk 1954 / Calder Hall 1956 / Shippingport 1957 = 11.5-15 yr; from NIF gain>1 (Dec 2022, bg) -> 2034.5-2038; from a magnetic Q>1 ~2027 -> 2038.5-2042. Driver: NIF yield 3.15 MJ (2022, bg) -> 8.6 MJ (2025) = +54%/yr; log(87)/log(1.54) = 10.3 yr -> ~2035. Discounted Helion 2028 (stated 2023): x1.5-3 -> 2030.5-2038. Prev ETA 2028 (undiscounted proponent date) given little weight. Working: ledger/staging/assess-fusion-20261006T142438Z/eta-notes.md
eta.cruxes: Earlier: Helion Polaris net electricity; Orion hardware installed on schedule 2026-27; SPARC first plasma and Q>1 (~2027). Later: Orion pause or PPA renegotiation; SPARC slipping past 2028; another missed Helion milestone; independent finding that D-He3 FRC gain is unattainable.

basis.path: Lead: Helion Orion (D-He3 pulsed FRC with direct energy recovery, Malaga WA), construction since July 2025, reactor-building permit Oct 2025 (legacy), PPA to Microsoft, >$1B raised, Polaris prototype operating (legacy). Next: CFS SPARC -> ARC (D-T tokamak, ~$3B raised, DOE-validated magnets, Google to buy half of ARC output); then TAE, Tokamak Energy, Focused Energy (Biblis). The milestone is tracked through these programmes' dates and the gain driver, since no grid-delivery series can exist before the first plant

Credibility: all dates are proponent projections; Helion already slipped one

label: Distant: no fusion LCOE yet; FOAK est. >$150/MWh vs <$100 goal; learning-curve ETA ~2056
rationale: No fusion plant runs, so fusion LCOE has no measured value; the only independent estimate puts first-of-a-kind plants above $150/MWh (Lindley et al. 2023, now verified), against the <$100/MWh goal and a ~$78/MWh gas combined-cycle average (Lazard 2025). Getting from ~$150-190 to <$100 needs roughly 3-5 Wright's-law doublings of fleet capacity after a first plant expected around 2035, which at offshore-wind-like learning (IRENA offshore LCOE 208 -> 79 $/MWh, 2010-2024) and build rates gives a median of ~2056 (80% range 2041 to never). That is over 10 years away: red (Distant).

basis.rule: Milestone red: median ETA 2056 > made_at + 10 years (Distant). Learning from a FOAK cost > $150/MWh needs a fleet that cannot exist before the first commercial plant (~2035); the only sub-$100 figure is a proponent projection, which cannot lift a status

eta.method: learning curve (Wright's law) on top of the First Watt forecast, Monte Carlo; cross-checked with reference class (offshore wind, fission) and a discounted proponent date
eta.calc: Gap: fusion LCOE unmeasured; FOAK > $150 (lindley-rv) vs < $100 = > 1.5x, ~1.9x at a fission-like FOAK $190 (Lazard new fission $142-222, gas CC avg $78: lazard-lcoe-2025-rv). Doublings n = ln(FOAK/100)/-ln(1-LR): gap 1.5 -> 3.85/2.91/1.82 at LR 10/13/20%; gap 2.0 -> 6.58/4.98/3.11. Year = first-watt year + 3 + n x Td. Deterministic (FOAK 2035, Td 2.5): 2042.5 (1.5x, 20%) / 2048.0 (1.75x, 13%) / 2054.4 (2x, 10%). MC (N=200k): first-watt draws (p50 2035.9), FOAK lognormal median $190 (80% $121-297), LR U(5-20%), Td U(2-4 yr), 20% fission-like no learning -> P(FOAK<100) 3%, p10 2042.3, p50 2059.6, P(2050) 28%; p50 sensitivity 2050.6-2057 (no-never branch 2055.0, FOAK $160 2054.6, Td 1.5-3 2054.9). Proxy calibration: IRENA offshore wind LCOE 208/155/127/89/81/79 (2010/15/18/20/22/24) = -6.7%/yr, crossed $100 ~2019.4; onshore -8.2%/yr, solar -15.0%/yr. Reference class (bg): offshore wind first farm 1991 -> < $100 2019 = 28 yr -> 2063; fission Shippingport 1957 -> competitive turnkey ~1963-67 = 6-10 yr -> 2041-45 (later reversed). Discounted CFS NOAK $50-100 (legacy, undated; implied ~2038, stated 2025) x1.5-3 -> 2044.5-2064. Prev ETA '>10 years, not estimable' (bucket). Working: ledger/staging/assess-fusion-20261006T142438Z/eta-notes.md
eta.cruxes: Earlier: an independent cost estimate below ~$120/MWh for a direct-conversion or aneutronic design; Orion delivering at its contracted price; ARC capital cost ($/kW) disclosed below fission; follow-on plant orders before the first plant runs. Later: FOAK capital cost at or above new fission; First Watt slipping past 2035; fission-like regulation of D-T tritium inventories; reading $100 as nominal (inflation erodes it).

basis.path: Proxy chain, since fusion LCOE has no series: (1) first commercial plant timing (The First Watt forecast, p50 2035: Helion Orion, CFS ARC); (2) Wright's-law cost decline from the FOAK estimate (> $150/MWh, Lindley 2023), with learning rates calibrated on offshore wind, the closest capital-intensive, site-built analogue in the ledger (IRENA LCOE series). LCOE of a new generation technology tracks capital cost per kW and capacity factor, both of which fall with cumulative build-out; fission is the cautionary counter-example (flat or negative learning)

label: Distant: no fusion LCOE yet; FOAK est. >$150/MWh vs <$100 goal; learning-curve ETA ~2045
rationale: No fusion plant runs, so fusion LCOE has no measured value; the only independent estimate puts first-of-a-kind plants above $150/MWh (Lindley et al. 2023), against the <$100/MWh goal and a ~$78/MWh gas combined-cycle average (Lazard 2025). Closing a ~1.7x gap takes about 2.4 Wright's-law doublings of fleet capacity at 8-20% learning (offshore wind measured ~18%), which can only start after a first plant forecast for ~2034; the Monte Carlo median is 2045 (80% range 2036 to never, the open end being fission-like no learning). A median over 10 years away is red (Distant).

basis.rule: Milestone red: median ETA 2045 > made_at + 10 years (Distant). Learning from a FOAK cost > $150/MWh needs a fleet that cannot exist before the first commercial plant (First Watt p50 2034); the only sub-$100 figure is a proponent projection, which cannot lift a status

eta.method: learning curve (Wright's law) on top of the First Watt forecast, Monte Carlo; cross-checked with reference classes (offshore wind, fission) and a discounted proponent figure
eta.calc: Gap: fusion LCOE unmeasured; FOAK > $150 (lindley-rv) vs < $100 -> >= 1.5x, ~1.7x at FOAK median $170 (inside Lindley's bound; new fission $142-222, gas CC avg $78: lazard-lcoe-2025-rv). n = ln(FOAK/100)/-log2(1-LR); year = FW + 2 (follow-on orders) + n x Td. Deterministic (FW 2034, Td 3): gap 1.5 -> n 2.67/2.10/1.26 at LR 10/12.5/20% -> 2044.0/2042.3/2039.8; gap 1.7 -> 2046.5/2044.3/2040.9; gap 1.9 -> 2048.7/2046.0/2042.0. MC (N=400k): FW 2027 + lognormal(median 7, p90 26 yr; floor 2029.5), FOAK lognormal median $170 (80% $116-249), LR U(8-20%), Td U(2-4) -> P(FOAK<100) 3.9%, p10 2036.1, p50 2044.8, p90 2064.5; sensitivities 2043.1-2049.5 (FOAK $150 2044.1, $190 2048.3; Td 1.5-3 2043.9, 3-5 2049.5). A 20% fission-like no-learning branch (neighbouring technology, no fusion cost evidence) only sets p90: with it p50 2047.8, P(by 2100) 0.79 -> p90 null. Calibration: IRENA offshore wind 208/155/127/89/81/79 $/MWh (2010-24) = -6.9%/yr; with ~3 -> ~83 GW cumulative (bg) LR 18%; ln(1.7)/0.069 = 7.7 yr after FW+2 -> 2043.7. Reference class (bg): fission Shippingport 1957 -> competitive turnkey 1963-67 = 6-10 yr -> 2040-44 (later reversed); offshore wind 1991 -> < $100 ~2019 = 28 yr -> 2062. CFS NOAK $50-100 (legacy) implies ~2038, x1.5-3 on 13 yr -> 2044.5-2064. Prev ETA p50 2056. Working: ledger/staging/assess-fusion-20261012T170615Z/eta-notes.md
eta.cruxes: Earlier: an independent post-2023 fusion LCOE study below ~$120/MWh (especially direct-conversion D-He3); the Helion-Microsoft PPA price disclosed below $100; Orion/ARC capital cost ($/kW) near gas CC; follow-on plant orders before the first plant runs. Later: FOAK capital cost at or above new fission; First Watt slipping past 2035; fission-like licensing of D-T tritium inventories; reading $100 as nominal.

basis.path: Proxy chain, since fusion LCOE has no series: (1) first commercial plant timing (The First Watt forecast, p50 2034: Helion Orion, CFS ARC); (2) Wright's-law cost decline from the FOAK estimate (> $150/MWh, Lindley 2023) with learning rates calibrated on offshore wind (IRENA LCOE series), the closest capital-intensive, site-built learner in the ledger. LCOE of a new generator tracks $/kW and capacity factor, both of which fall with cumulative build-out; fission is the counter-example (flat or negative learning) and sets the open upper end
blockers: Technical (precursor missing): no fusion device has delivered net electricity, so no plant cost data exist
Economic: independent FOAK estimate > $150/MWh is above the $100 goal and gas CC (~$78/MWh avg, Lazard 2025)
Gather request: plant capital costs for Orion and ARC; independent fusion LCOE studies after 2023; Helion-Microsoft PPA price if disclosed

label: Progressing: no fusion on any grid; Helion Orion being built, no net electricity yet, ETA ~2034
rationale: No fusion plant delivers electricity to a grid and no device has shown net electricity (Helion missed its 2024 target), but Helion has been building its Orion plant since July 2025 and five funded programmes target commercial power for 2028-2035. Discounting those dates by the ~2x slip measured on Helion, ITER and CFS and taking the first success gives a median of 2033.3, which the fission reference class (chain reaction to grid power in 11.5-15 years, 2034.5-2038 from NIF ignition) pulls to ~2034 (80% range 2030-2053); unevidenced concept-failure odds only widen the range. A median within 10 years with measurable progress is yellow; it is not green because the median is beyond 5 years and there is no net-electricity precursor or independent corroboration.

basis.rule: Milestone yellow: measurable progress (first commercial plant under construction, record fusion gain, funded programmes) and median ETA 2034 <= made_at + 10 years. Not green: median > 5 years, no demonstrated precursor at relevant scale (no net electricity from any device), no non-proponent corroboration. Not achieved: no verified achievement of fusion electricity on a grid

eta.method: discounted proponent dates (first-success Monte Carlo over 5 funded programmes, slip factor calibrated on ledger slips) + structural floors, weighted with a reference class (fission); driver trend (NIF gain) as cross-check
eta.calc: Gap: 0 MWh fusion on any grid; no net electricity yet (helion-missed-2024-rv); best gain NIF Q=4.13 (8.6/2.08 MJ, nif-q-4-13-rv); ST40 triple product ~8e18 vs ~3e21 ignition (bg) = ~375x (tokamak-energy-st40-records-rv). Slip factor measured: Helion 2024 net electricity (stated 2021, bg) still open at 2026.78 -> >=1.93x; ITER first plasma 2025->2034 (iter-baseline-rv, 2016 baseline) = 2.0x; CFS SPARC ~1.3x (bg) -> median 2x. MC (N=400k): year = stated + (target-stated) x F, F lognormal median 2x (shared sd 0.25, own 0.30), floors Helion 2029, CFS/TAE 2031, Tokamak Energy 2032, Biblis 2033; programmes Helion 2028 (stated 2023.4), CFS ARC ~2032.5, TAE ~2032.5, Tokamak Energy ~2035.5, Biblis 2035 (stated 2025) -> first-of-any p10 2029.6, p50 2033.3, p90 2038.7; F 1.5x/3x -> p50 2031.0/2038.1. Concept-failure odds (0.4-0.75) have no measuring evidence -> range only: p10 2030.8, p50 2036.6, p90 2053.3. Reference class (bg): CP-1 1942 -> Obninsk 1954/Calder Hall 1956/Shippingport 1957 = 11.5-15 yr -> 2034.5-2038 from NIF gain>1 (Dec 2022). p50 = 2/3 x 2033.3 + 1/3 x 2036 = 2034.2 -> 2034 (+0.7 yr from the reference class only). Driver: NIF gain 0.72 (2021, bg) -> 4.13 (2025) = x1.61/yr; laser plant gain 30-100 in 4.1-6.7 yr (2029-2032), so build/rep-rate, not physics gain, binds. Discounted Helion 2028 x1.5/2/3 -> 2031.1/2033.6/2038.7; CFS ARC -> 2036.3/2040.0/2047.5. Prev ETA p50 2035 (MC 2035.9, failure odds in median). Working: ledger/staging/assess-fusion-20261012T170615Z/eta-notes.md
eta.cruxes: Earlier: Helion Polaris net electricity or published gain; Orion generator hardware installed 2026-27; SPARC first plasma and Q>1 (~2027); a disclosed Orion interconnection date. Later: Orion paused or Microsoft PPA renegotiated; another missed Helion milestone; SPARC slipping past 2028; independent evidence that D-He3 FRC gain is unattainable (moves weight to ARC ~2040).

basis.path: Lead: Helion Orion (D-He3 pulsed FRC with direct energy recovery, Malaga WA): construction since July 2025, reactor-building permit Oct 2025 (legacy), Microsoft PPA, >$1B raised, Polaris prototype operating (legacy). Next: CFS SPARC -> ARC (D-T tokamak, ~$3B raised, DOE-validated magnets, Google to buy half of output); then TAE, Tokamak Energy, Focused Energy at Biblis. Grid delivery has no series before a first plant, so the milestone is tracked through these programmes' slip-discounted dates, the fission reference class and the NIF gain driver
blockers: Technical (precursor missing): no device has demonstrated net electricity; Helion missed its 2024 net-electricity target
Credibility: all dates are proponent projections; Helion already slipped one and ITER slipped ~9 years
Technical (D-T paths): tritium breeding and neutron-resistant materials unproven at scale; ITER D-T operation 2039
Gather request: Helion Polaris results and Orion construction status; SPARC commissioning; NIF shot yields 2021-2026 as a ledger series
